subject: RetailZen POC charter & model pathway — acceptance criteria and next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam Turner <liam.turner@retailzen.com>, Alex Novak <alex.novak@retailzen.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: RetailZen POC recap & proposed charter (models, metrics, ownership)

Thanks for the call earlier today — really great to understand the customer-facing flows and the latency/cost sensitivity for peak traffic. Summary and proposed next steps below so we have a single source of truth.

Key highlights from discovery:
- Primary use: conversational product recommendations and short personalized product descriptions (mainly English; Spanish for ~12% of traffic).
- Target throughput: bursty 40–60 req/s during campaign windows, baseline ~8–12 req/s.
- Quality bar: human-preference rating >85% on seed prompts; no high-severity factual hallucinations on SKU data.
- Security: standard SOC 2 / audit requirements, potential need for private deployment if procurement insists.

Proposed POC (3-week phased):
Phase 1 (Week 0–1): baseline pass — integrate SDK, upload eval seed sets, run initial generation tests.
Phase 2 (Week 1–2): performance tuning — batching, KV-cache warmup, measure p95 latency & cost per token.
Phase 3 (Week 2–3): acceptance scoring — run blind human preference evals, apply multilingual checks.

Model recommendations for the trial (proposed primary + fallback):
- Primary: Llama-3-13B (q4f) — best tradeoff for English generation quality at moderate cost.
- Fallback: Mistral-7B-Instruct (int8) — lower cost, good latency for degraded capacity or cost-capped routing.
- Multilingual approach: evaluate both on English + Spanish seed sets; if Spanish fails quality thresholds, evaluate a Spanish-specialist variant (we'll surface options).

Proposed acceptance criteria (draft):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation < 350 ms for single-turn queries at 1–2 token-k limits (target for default routing).
- Throughput: sustain 50 req/s for 30 seconds without error spike (can use Dedicated for stability).
- Quality: human-preference win-rate >= 85% vs. current baseline on curated prompt set; factual correctness flag rate < 2% on SKU lookups.
- Multilingual: Spanish preference score >= 80% on bilingual seed set.
- Cost target: average token cost < $0.0025 per output token (tunable with batching/quant).

Owners:
- Retail contact/POC: Liam Turner (confirm).
- Redwood PM: Grace O'Connor (program lead).
- Redwood Tech lead: Ben Carter (benchmarking, infra config).

Requested from RetailZen to get started:
1) Confirmation on the seed prompt set or upload of 200–300 sample queries (English + Spanish).
2) Point of contact for procurement/security and any constraints on environment (SaaS vs VPC).
3) A short list of 10 high-priority SKUs for factualness checks.

Attachments: RetailZen_POC_Charter_v1.xlsx (charter + timeline), eval_seedset_en_es.csv (sample prompts).

If the model choices above look good, we'll schedule a short kickoff (30–45m) next week and spin up the sandbox. If procurement will require SOC2 evidence first, let me know and I'll loop in our security lead.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0123

From: Liam Turner <liam.turner@retailzen.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Novak <alex.novak@retailzen.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Procurement <procurement@retailzen.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RetailZen POC recap & proposed charter (models, metrics, ownership)

Thanks Grace — this is very helpful and aligns with our internal expectations. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

1) Procurement will likely ask for SOC 2 Type II evidence before we sign any plug-and-play SLA. Can you provide a pointer to the report or a short compliance pack?
2) For the POC, do you recommend hosted Redwood or a private VPC for the initial run? We prefer hosted for speed but procurement may push for private.
3) Can you confirm whether the suggested models will preserve PII redaction settings out of the box? We have customer emails in some prompts and need guaranteed redaction controls.

I've attached a short procurement timeline (procurement_timeline.pdf) that shows a target internal approval window of ~3 weeks. If we can keep the POC to 3 weeks and produce results, that's ideal.

I'll confirm the RetailZen POC contact (I'll be the business lead) and loop in Alex for product-level details.

— Liam
Liam Turner
Head of Product | RetailZen
liam.turner@retailzen.com

---
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam Turner <liam.turner@retailzen.com>, Alex Novak <alex.novak@retailzen.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Procurement <procurement@retailzen.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2026 12:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RetailZen POC recap & proposed charter (models, metrics, ownership)

Great — answers inline and a slightly revised plan.

1) SOC2 / compliance: yes, we can share our SOC 2 pack and a short compliance briefing doc. I'll attach a redacted pack and loop in our security contact if procurement needs live review.

2) Hosted vs VPC: recommendation is hosted Redwood API for the initial POC for fastest time-to-value. If procurement requires private controls we can run the same charter in a private VPC during Phase 2 (seamless from a config perspective). We'll note this as a conditional requirement in the charter.

3) PII redaction: our runtime supports token-level redaction markers and a configurable PII filter pipeline. For the POC we'll enable redaction rules and include a small precision/recall check on masked content in Phase 1. If you need certification on retention, we can add a data flow diagram to the compliance pack.

Model specifics and fallback logic:
- Primary: Llama-3-13B (q4f). We'll run the model with prefix caching and default batch size of 4 for latency tests.
- Fallback: Mistral-7B-Instruct (int8) — used automatically when cost or latency routing thresholds hit.
- Routing policy: start with quality-first routing (primary model), enable cost-fallback for synthetic load tests. We will provide cost delta estimates after initial benchmarks.

Acceptance criteria (finalized for charter):
- p95 latency < 350 ms (single-turn median prompt length).
- Sustain 50 req/s for 30s with error rate < 0.5%.
- Human-preference >= 85% (blind eval) vs baseline.
- Spanish seed set preference >= 80%.
- Cost delta to baseline <= 30% (we'll calculate after bench).

Attachments included: RetailZen_POC_Charter_v1.xlsx (charter + timeline), eval_seedset_en_es.csv (300 sample prompts), model_benchmarks_q4.pdf (initial microbenchmarks).

Next steps/action items:
- Liam: confirm POC lead and share 200–300 sample queries + 10 priority SKUs by EOD Wed (Jun 2).
- Alex: if any product constraints on prompt length or tokenization, flag now.
- Procurement: review SOC2 pack (I attached a short packet) and confirm whether the hosted option is permitted for a 3-week POC.
- Ben: I'll hand off tech onboarding to you for sandbox infra and perf testing.

I'll schedule a 30-minute kickoff Wed or Thu — please indicate preferred slots.

Thanks all,
Grace

---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Liam Turner <liam.turner@retailzen.com>
Cc: Alex Novak <alex.novak@retailzen.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RetailZen POC recap & proposed charter (models, metrics, ownership)

Thanks Grace — quick technical notes from my side before the kickoff:

- KV cache warmup: for product-description flows we recommend a small synthetic warmup (20–30 queries) prior to measurement to avoid cold-start p95 spikes. We'll automate that in the benchmark harness.
- Batch sizing: start at batch=4 for latency testing; for cost testing we'll iterate to batch=8/16 depending on GPU availability.
- Spanish behavior: early Mistral variants can underperform on idiomatic Spanish; we'll surface a Spanish-specialist open model if score < 80% after Phase 1.
- Monitoring hooks: I'll drop a short JSON schema for the metrics we need (latency/p95, error rate, token cost, human-eval links).

Attached microbenchmarks show expected p95 ranges (see model_benchmarks_q4.pdf). I'll own the infra checklist and will share a sandbox invite once Liam confirms the sample seed sets.

See you at kickoff.
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
